title: 1979 Paris–Dakar Rally
who: Won by Alain Génestier (Range Rover) and Cyril Neveu (Yamaha XT500)
summary: The 1979 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 19 stage towns and bivouacs through France, Algeria, Niger, Mali, Senegal. Winners — Cars: Alain Génestier (Range Rover); Bikes: Cyril Neveu (Yamaha XT500).
approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Paris
stops.text: The start of the first Paris–Dakar: 182 competitors (80 cars, 90 bikes, 12 trucks) leave the Place du Trocadéro on Boxing Day.

stops.name: Montlhéry
stops.text: Bivouac after stage 1's short opening special at the Montlhéry circuit, 3.6 km.

stops.name: Marseille
stops.text: A liaison south through France to the port; then three days' transport across the Mediterranean.

stops.name: Algiers
stops.text: Back on land in Africa: stage 2 starts with a long liaison south into the Sahara.

stops.name: Reggane
stops.text: Bivouac on stage 2, deep in the Algerian Sahara.

stops.name: In Salah
stops.text: New Year's Day: a 270 km special from Reggane to In Salah, still stage 2.

stops.name: Tamanrasset
stops.text: A liaison down to Tamanrasset in the Hoggar mountains, the end of stage 2.

stops.name: In Guezzam
stops.text: Stage 3 begins: a 373 km special to In Guezzam, the last Algerian post before Niger.

stops.name: Assamaka
stops.text: Across the border: the day's 230 km special starts at the Niger frontier post.

stops.name: Arlit
stops.text: Bivouac at the uranium-mining town of Arlit, still stage 3.

stops.name: Agadez
stops.text: The 231 km Arlit–Agadez special, where about a quarter of the field got lost, early leader Christophe Neveu among them.

stops.name: Niamey
stops.text: Stage 4: 230 km timed on the way south-west to Niger's capital.

stops.name: Gao
stops.text: Stage 5 into Mali; its special was cancelled. A rest day in Gao followed.

stops.name: Mopti
stops.text: Stage 6: a 600 km special along the Niger, won among the cars by Alain Génestier.

stops.name: Bamako
stops.text: A liaison to Mali's capital to end stage 6.

stops.name: Nioro du Sahel
stops.text: Stage 7: 417 km to Nioro du Sahel, a stage so hard its time limit was extended.

stops.name: Kayes
stops.text: Stage 8 begins with a 270 km special to Kayes.

stops.name: Bakel
stops.text: Across the Senegal river into Senegal for the last night.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish after a final 96 km special. 74 of 182 starters made it; Cyril Neveu won on a Yamaha XT500 without winning a single stage.
